newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC CLOSE GAP ON RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC CLOSE GAP ON RANGERS.

text.p: Celtic narrowed the gap on Rangers at the top of the Scottish premier division to 11 points with two games in hand on Saturday after bouncing back to beat Dunfermline 4-2 before nearly 46,000 fans at Parkhead.
Rangers' match at Kilmarnock was postponed because of freezing weather.
Celtic survived an early scare when their former player Gerry Britton headed the visitors ahead after only six minutes.

Celtic had to wait until the 35th minute before Portuguese forward Jorge Cadete equalised and within 25 minutes Celtic were 4-1 up with further goals from Dutchman Pierre Van Hooydonk, Cadete again and Simon Donnelly. Britton scored a second for Dunfermline in the 68th minute.

Third-placed Aberdeen needed a last-minute equaliser from Duncan Shearer to force a 1-1 draw at home to Hibernian. Hearts were the other big winners of the day, beating Motherwell 4-1. John Robertson scored twice, once from the spot, and David Weir and James Hamilton added the others. Tommy Coyne had given Motherwell the lead after 12 minutes.
There was no joy for bottom-placed Raith who were beaten 1-0 at home by Dundee United.
